transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hi, I'm Dora, your clinical conversational agent. I'm here to answer any questions you may have about your cataract surgery recovery. Do you have any questions for me today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do have a few questions. When can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
You should avoid any exercise for 1 week after surgery. After that, you can go back to light exercise, such as brisk walking, gardening, light jogging, and gentle cycling. However, you should avoid strenuous, heavy exercise, lifting heavy objects, pilates or yoga, or swimming for a month.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
If you were using any eye drops before your operation, such as for glaucoma or for dry eyes, it's safe to continue using them, unless you've been told otherwise.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
It's normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to the new lenses. However, if you have significant pain when it's bright or severe light sensitivity, especially if your eye is also red and painful, that is not normal and may need to be assessed. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside.

Do you have any other questions?

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, I don't have any more questions. Thank you for your help!

transcript.speaker: patient
